title: Dehydration in Children: Clinical Assessment
subject: Pediatrics
preview: Children with dehydration may have reduced urine output, dry mucosae, sunken eyes, thirst or altered activity.
quickRevision: Children with dehydration may have reduced urine output, dry mucosae, sunken eyes, thirst or altered activity.
Oral rehydration is suitable for many mild to moderate cases when the child can drink; severe illness needs urgent supervised treatment.
Fluid plans account for ongoing losses, age and comorbidity.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Children with dehydration may have reduced urine output, dry mucosae, sunken eyes, thirst or altered activity.
Assess mental status, capillary refill, pulse, breathing and ability to drink rather than relying only on skin turgor.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Oral rehydration is suitable for many mild to moderate cases when the child can drink; severe illness needs urgent supervised treatment.
Fluid plans account for ongoing losses, age and comorbidity.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A single sign does not precisely quantify dehydration severity in every child.

quiz.question: Which finding supports clinically significant dehydration?
quiz.explanation: Reduced urine output with lethargy. Children with dehydration may have reduced urine output, dry mucosae, sunken eyes, thirst or altered activity.
